task.title: Run the web editor
task.shortdesc: The web editor is an optional service on its own host. It signs authors in with GitHub or your company's identity provider, and commits for them through your GitHub App.

ul.li: A running server, with the docs repository registered and the GitHub App installed on it (installationId set). See .
A host name for the editor that is not the docs site's, such as edit.docs.example.com. Cookies ignore ports, so in production a different port on the same host is refused.

step.cmd: Give the GitHub App the permissions the editor needs, and accept the change on the installation.

strow.stentry: Reading files, saving commits, merging the main branch in
Opening, updating and merging pull requests
Read (keep Read and write for build statuses)
Checking a developer's permission on the repository

info.p: Without Administration read the editor still works, but it cannot see the review rules, so it never merges by itself: a maintainer merges each pull request on GitHub.

step.cmd: Set up at least one way to sign in.

choices.choice: GitHub, for developers: create an OAuth app (or use the GitHub App's own client id and secret) with the callback URL $EDITOR_PUBLIC_URL/auth/github/callback. Anyone with write, maintain or admin permission on the docs repository gets an account the first time they sign in.

Company OIDC, for other authors: register a client with your identity provider, with the redirect URI $EDITOR_PUBLIC_URL/auth/oidc/callback. It can be the same provider as reader sign-in, but use a separate client. These authors must be added before they can sign in.

info.p: The editor reads its own settings and checks them all at start-up. It shares DATABASE_URL and the GitHub App with the other services, but never the session secret.

property.propdesc: The same Postgres database as the docs site.

choices.choice: Docker Compose: docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --profile editor up -d starts the editor service on port 3001 (or OPEND_EDITOR_PORT). Put it behind your reverse proxy on its own host name.

Railway: add a third service, editor, from the same repository and deploy/Dockerfile, with the start command node dist/bin.js editor serve, the health check /healthz and its own public domain on port 3000. It needs no pre-deploy step: the web service runs the migrations. See .
Anywhere else: run opend-server editor serve from the image.

step.cmd: Add the authors who sign in with their company account.

stepxmp.codeblock: opend-server editor add-user writer@example.com --name "Wendy Writer" opend-server editor add-user dev@example.com --github dev-login opend-server editor list-users opend-server editor disable-user writer@example.com

info.p: These commands need only DATABASE_URL. With Compose, run them as docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm migrate editor add-user ….

ul.li: add-user registers an email address, with the name used on commits. --github also lets that GitHub account in, for developers without write access. Adding a disabled editor again turns them back on.
Company accounts are matched by verified email at first sign-in, then by the provider's subject.
disable-user stops someone signing in and ends their sessions at once.

result.p: Authors sign in at EDITOR_PUBLIC_URL. See for what they can do.

ul.li: Edit this page. Set EDITOR_PUBLIC_URL on the docs site too, and signed-in readers see Edit this page under each topic, opening /edit?path=topic file in the editor. The editor still asks them to sign in as an author. One GitHub App can serve both hosts; see .
Separate accounts. Editors are not readers. A reader session never opens the editor, and an editor session grants nothing on the docs site.

Commits. Each save is a commit by the App to the author's branch editor/<user-id>/<name>, with the author's name and email and a Co-authored-by line. The editor refuses to write to any other branch, including the main branch.

Preview as an org. Any signed-in editor can preview their branch as an org that has entitlements. Each preview is tied to that editor, one commit and the org's entitlements at that moment, expires after 30 minutes, and is logged. There are no editor roles yet.

Audit. Every sign-in, save, merge from the main branch, conflict resolution, publish, merge, request for a developer and preview is recorded in the editor_audit table, with the session, user, commit and pull request. Each author sees their own on the Activity page.
Large repositories. The preview rebuilds the whole docs project in memory. That suits hundreds of topics; a repository too large for GitHub's recursive tree listing is refused.
